statement:
theorem lemma1 {A : Type} [CommRing A] [DecidableEq A] {I : Ideal A}
    (hInonfg : ¬I.FG) (n : ℕ) (g : ∀ m, m < n → I) :
    Set.Nonempty
      ((I : Set A) \
        Ideal.span (Finset.image (fun m : Fin n => (g m.1 m.2).1) Finset.univ :
          Set A))
proof:
:= by
  rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
  intro h
  rw [Set.diff_eq_empty] at h
  apply hInonfg
  refine' ⟨Finset.image (fun m : Fin n => (g m.1 m.2).1) Finset.univ, _⟩
  refine' le_antisymm _ h
  rw [Ideal.span_le]
  intro a ha
  simp only [Finset.coe_image, Finset.coe_univ, Set.image_univ,
    Set.mem_range] at ha
  rcases ha with ⟨y, rfl⟩
  exact (g y.1 y.2).2

name: lemma1'
proof:
:= by

  set S : Set A := _
  have ne1 : Set.Nonempty S := lemma1 hInonfg n g

  choose x hx using ne1
  refine ⟨⟨x, hx.1⟩, ?_⟩
  simp only [Finset.coe_image, Finset.coe_univ, Set.image_univ, Set.mem_diff,
    SetLike.mem_coe, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hx ⊢
  exact hx.2

proof:
:= by
  have := (Nat.prime_iff_fac_equiv_neg_one (?_ : p ≠ 1)).1 hp
  · rw [← this, hn]
    norm_cast
    congr
    simp

name: exists_sqrt_neg_one_of_one_mod_four
statement:
theorem exists_sqrt_neg_one_of_one_mod_four
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hp2 : ∃ n, p = 4 * n + 1) :
    ∃ i : ZMod p, i ^ 2 = -1
proof:
:= by
  cases' hp2 with n hn
  set i := ∏ j in Finset.Icc 1 (2 * n), (j : ZMod p) with hi
  have h1 : ∏ j in Finset.Icc 1 (2 * n), (-1 : ZMod p) = 1
  · rw [Finset.prod_const]
    simp only [Nat.add_succ_sub_one, add_zero, Nat.card_Icc]
    rw [pow_mul, neg_one_pow_two, one_pow]
  have h2 : ∏ j in Finset.Icc 1 (2 * n), (-j : ZMod p) = i
  · conv_lhs => rhs; ext; rw [neg_eq_neg_one_mul]
    rw [Finset.prod_mul_distrib, h1, one_mul]
  have h3 : ∏ j in Finset.Icc (2 * n + 1) (4 * n), (j : ZMod p) = i
  · rw [← h2]
    apply Finset.prod_bij' (fun j _ => p - j) (fun j _ => p - j)  <;>
    rintro a ha <;>
    rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at *
    rotate_right
    suffices : a + (p - a) = p
    · rw [eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero]
      norm_cast
      simp [this]
    all_goals omega
  use i
  rw [pow_two]
  nth_rw 1 [hi]
  rw [← h3]
  rw [← Finset.prod_union]
  · convert_to ∏ j in Finset.Icc 1 (4 * n), (j : ZMod p) = -1
    · congr
      ext x
      rw [Finset.mem_union]
      simp only [Finset.mem_Icc]
      constructor <;>
      · intros
        omega
    · apply wilson_theorem hp hn
  · rw [disjoint_iff_inf_le]
    rintro x (hx : x ∈ _ ∩ _)
    rw [Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_Icc, Finset.mem_Icc] at hx
    rcases hx with ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _, _⟩
    linarith

theorem infinite_iff_arb_large (S : Set ℕ) :
    S.Infinite ↔ ∀ N, ∃ n > N, n ∈ S
proof:
:= by
  constructor
  · intro h n
    have h2 := Set.Infinite.exists_not_mem_finset h (Finset.range (n + 1))
    rcases h2 with ⟨m, hm, h3⟩
    use m
    refine' ⟨_, hm⟩
    contrapose! h3
    exact Finset.mem_range_succ_iff.mpr h3
  · contrapose!
    intro h
    rw [Set.not_infinite] at h
    let S2 : Finset ℕ := Set.Finite.toFinset h
    have h2 : ∃ B, ∀ n ∈ S2, n ≤ B := by
      use Finset.sup S2 id
      intros _ H
      apply Finset.le_sup H
    cases' h2 with N hN
    use N
    have h3 : ∀ n : ℕ, n ∈ S ↔ n ∈ S2
    intro n
    exact (Set.Finite.mem_toFinset h).symm
    intro n hn h4
    rw [h3] at h4
    specialize hN n h4
    linarith

name: you
statement:
lemma you need about filters. In fact we'll also be using a bunch of
stuff about sets, like `Set.inter_subset_left`, so why don't we `open Set`
as well.
-/

section Section12Sheet1Solutions

open Filter Set




variable (α : Type) (F : Filter α) (S T : Set α)

/-
Here's a lemma about filters: Two sets `S` and `T` are both in
a filter `F` if and only if their intersection is. See if you can deduce
it from the axioms of a filter.

For this one it's useful to know the following results (from the set namespace)
`inter_subset_left S T : S ∩ T ⊆ S`
and
`inter_subset_right S T : S ∩ T ⊆ S`
-/
example : S ∩ T ∈ F ↔ S ∈ F ∧ T ∈ F
proof:
:= by
  constructor
  · intro hST
    constructor
    · apply mem_of_superset hST
      exact inter_subset_left S T
    · apply mem_of_superset hST
      exact inter_subset_right S T
  · rintro ⟨hS, hT⟩
    exact inter_mem hS hT

name: mul_left_cancel
statement: theorem mul_left_cancel (h : a * b = a * c) : b = c
proof:
:=
  calc
    b = 1 * b := by rw [one_mul]
    _ = a⁻¹ * a * b := by rw [inv_mul_self]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (a * b) := by rw [mul_assoc]
    _ = a⁻¹ * (a * c) := by rw [h]
    _ = a⁻¹ * a * c := by rw [mul_assoc]
    _ = 1 * c := by rw [inv_mul_self]
    _ = c := by rw [one_mul]

statement: theorem mul_eq_of_eq_inv_mul (h : b = a⁻¹ * c) : a * b = c
proof:

  rwa [← mul_assoc, inv_mul_self, one_mul]

statement:
theorem tendsTo_add {a b : ℕ → ℝ} {t u : ℝ} (ha : TendsTo a t) (hb : TendsTo b u) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n + b n) (t + u)
proof:
:=
  by
  rw [tendsTo_def] at *
  
  intro ε hε
  
  specialize ha (ε / 2) (by linarith)
  cases' ha with X hX
  
  obtain ⟨Y, hY⟩ := hb (ε / 2) (by linarith)
  
  use max X Y
  
  intro n hn
  rw [max_le_iff] at hn
  specialize hX n hn.1
  specialize hY n hn.2
  
  rw [abs_lt] at *
  constructor <;>
    linarith

name: tendsTo_sub
statement:
theorem tendsTo_sub {a b : ℕ → ℝ} {t u : ℝ} (ha : TendsTo a t) (hb : TendsTo b u) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n - b n) (t - u)
proof:
:= by
  simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using tendsTo_add ha (tendsTo_neg hb)

name: tendsTo_def
statement:
theorem tendsTo_def {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} :
    TendsTo a t ↔ ∀ ε, 0 < ε → ∃ B : ℕ, ∀ n, B ≤ n → |a n - t| < ε

name: tendsTo_thirtyseven
statement: theorem tendsTo_thirtyseven : TendsTo (fun n ↦ 37) 37
proof:
:=
  by
  rw [tendsTo_def]
  intro ε hε
  use 100
  intro n hn
  norm_num
  exact hε

name: tendsTo_const
statement: theorem tendsTo_const (c : ℝ) : TendsTo (fun n => c) c
proof:
:=
  by
  intro ε hε
  dsimp only
  use 37
  intro n hn
  ring_nf
  norm_num
  exact hε

name: tendsTo_add_const
statement:
theorem tendsTo_add_const {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (h : TendsTo a t) :
    TendsTo (fun n => a n + c) (t + c)
proof:
:=
  by
  rw [tendsTo_def] at h ⊢
  ring_nf
  exact h

name: tendsTo_thirtyseven_mul
statement:
theorem tendsTo_thirtyseven_mul (a : ℕ → ℝ) (t : ℝ) (h : TendsTo a t) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ 37 * a n) (37 * t)
proof:
:= by
  intro ε hε
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := h (ε / 37) (by linarith)
  use X
  intro n hn
  specialize hX n hn
  simp
  rw [← mul_sub, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg] <;> linarith

name: tendsTo_pos_const_mul
statement:
theorem tendsTo_pos_const_mul {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (h : TendsTo a t) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ c * a n) (c * t)
proof:
:= by
  intro ε hε
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := h (ε / c) (div_pos hε hc)
  use X
  intro n hn
  specialize hX n hn
  simp
  rw [← mul_sub, abs_mul, abs_of_pos hc]
  exact (lt_div_iff' hc).mp hX

name: tendsTo_neg_const_mul
statement:
theorem tendsTo_neg_const_mul {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (h : TendsTo a t) {c : ℝ} (hc : c < 0) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ c * a n) (c * t)
proof:
:=
  by
  have hc' : 0 < -c := neg_pos.mpr hc
  intro ε hε
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := h (ε / -c) (div_pos hε hc')
  use X
  intro n hn
  specialize hX n hn
  simp
  rw [← mul_sub, abs_mul, abs_of_neg hc]
  exact (lt_div_iff' hc').mp hX

name: tendsTo_const_mul
statement:
theorem tendsTo_const_mul {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (h : TendsTo a t) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ c * a n) (c * t)
proof:
:=
  by
  obtain hc | rfl | hc := lt_trichotomy 0 c
  · exact tendsTo_pos_const_mul h hc
  · simpa using tendsTo_const 0
  · exact tendsTo_neg_const_mul h hc

name: tendsTo_mul_const
statement:
theorem tendsTo_mul_const {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (h : TendsTo a t) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n * c) (t * c)
proof: := by simpa [mul_comm] using tendsTo_const_mul c h

name: tendsTo_neg'
statement: theorem tendsTo_neg' {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} (ha : TendsTo a t) : TendsTo (fun n ↦ -a n) (-t)

name: tendsTo_of_tendsTo_sub
statement:
theorem tendsTo_of_tendsTo_sub {a b : ℕ → ℝ} {t u : ℝ} (h1 : TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n - b n) t)
    (h2 : TendsTo b u) : TendsTo a (t + u)
proof: := by simpa using tendsTo_add h1 h2

name: tendsTo_sub_lim_iff
statement: theorem tendsTo_sub_lim_iff {a : ℕ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} : TendsTo a t ↔ TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n - t) 0
proof:
:=
  by
  constructor
  · intro h
    simpa using tendsTo_sub h (tendsTo_const t)
  · intro h
    simpa using tendsTo_add h (tendsTo_const t)

name: tendsTo_zero_mul_tendsTo_zero
statement:
theorem tendsTo_zero_mul_tendsTo_zero {a b : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : TendsTo a 0) (hb : TendsTo b 0) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n * b n) 0
proof:
:= by
  intro ε hε
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := ha ε hε
  obtain ⟨Y, hY⟩ := hb 1 zero_lt_one
  use max X Y
  intro n hn
  specialize hX n (le_of_max_le_left hn)
  specialize hY n (le_of_max_le_right hn)
  simpa [abs_mul] using mul_lt_mul'' hX hY

name: tendsTo_mul
statement:
theorem tendsTo_mul (a b : ℕ → ℝ) (t u : ℝ) (ha : TendsTo a t) (hb : TendsTo b u) :
    TendsTo (fun n ↦ a n * b n) (t * u)
proof:
:=
  by
  
  rw [tendsTo_sub_lim_iff] at *
  
  have h : ∀ n, a n * b n - t * u = (a n - t) * (b n - u) + t * (b n - u) + (a n - t) * u := by
    intro n; ring
  simp [h]
  rw [show (0 : ℝ) = 0 + t * 0 + 0 * u by simp]
  refine' tendsTo_add (tendsTo_add _ _) _
  · exact tendsTo_zero_mul_tendsTo_zero ha hb
  · exact tendsTo_const_mul t hb
  · exact tendsTo_mul_const u ha

name: tendsTo_unique
statement: theorem tendsTo_unique (a : ℕ → ℝ) (s t : ℝ) (hs : TendsTo a s) (ht : TendsTo a t) : s = t
proof:
:=
  by
  by_contra h
  wlog h2 : s < t
  · cases' Ne.lt_or_lt h with h3 h3
    · contradiction
    · apply this _ _ _ ht hs _ h3
      exact ne_comm.mp h
  set ε := t - s with hε
  have hε : 0 < ε := sub_pos.mpr h2
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := hs (ε / 2) (by linarith)
  obtain ⟨Y, hY⟩ := ht (ε / 2) (by linarith)
  specialize hX (max X Y) (le_max_left X Y)
  specialize hY (max X Y) (le_max_right X Y)
  rw [abs_lt] at hX hY
  linarith

name: eq_zero_of_abs_lt_eps
statement: theorem eq_zero_of_abs_lt_eps {r : ℝ} (h : ∀ ε > 0, |r| < ε) : r = 0
proof:
:=
  by
  
  by_contra h2
  
  specialize h |r| (abs_pos.mpr h2)
  
  linarith

name: tendsTo_unique'
statement: theorem tendsTo_unique' (a : ℕ → ℝ) (s t : ℝ) (hs : TendsTo a s) (ht : TendsTo a t) : s = t
proof:
:=
  by
  
  have h := tendsTo_sub hs ht
  
  
  suffices ∀ ε > 0, |t - s| < ε by linarith [eq_zero_of_abs_lt_eps this]
  
  intro ε hε
  
  obtain ⟨X, hX⟩ := h ε hε
  specialize hX X (by rfl)
  
  simpa using hX

name: Ideal.mem_iff_associated
statement:
theorem Ideal.mem_iff_associated {R : Type} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) {a b : R}
    (hab : Associated a b) : a ∈ I ↔ b ∈ I
proof:
:= by
  rcases hab with ⟨u, rfl⟩
  refine' ⟨I.mul_mem_right _, _⟩
  intro h
  convert I.mul_mem_right ((u⁻¹ : Rˣ) : R) h
  simp

name: Ideal.IsPrime.not_one_mem
statement:
theorem Ideal.IsPrime.not_one_mem
    {R : Type} [CommRing R] {P : Ideal R} (hI : P.IsPrime) :
    (1 : R) ∉ P
proof:
:= by
  intro h
  apply hI.ne_top
  rwa [Ideal.eq_top_iff_one]

name: Ideal.IsPrime.mem_of_prod_mem
statement:
theorem Ideal.IsPrime.mem_of_prod_mem
    {R : Type} [CommRing R] {P : Ideal R} (hP : P.IsPrime) {L : Multiset R} :
    L.prod ∈ P → ∃ x : R, x ∈ L ∧ x ∈ P
proof:
:= by
  refine L.induction_on ?_ ?_
  · intro h
    rw [Multiset.prod_zero] at h
    cases hP.not_one_mem h
  · intro a L IH h
    simp only [Multiset.prod_cons] at h
    rcases hP.mem_or_mem h with (ha | hL)
    · exact ⟨a, by simp, ha⟩
    · obtain ⟨x, hxL, hxP⟩ := IH hL
      exact ⟨x, Multiset.mem_cons_of_mem hxL, hxP⟩

name: Prime.ideal_span_singleton_isPrime
statement:
theorem Prime.ideal_span_singleton_isPrime
    {R : Type} [CommRing R] {p : R} (hp : Prime p) :
    (Ideal.span {p} : Ideal R).IsPrime
